a.text: New red wheat seeds, a burdenbeast saddle
Mill operation unit, looking for previously owned
Two woolen coats, Swinton's tailorshop, dad's needs its hem trimmed short.
(crossed out) (I said, I forgot)
Grab some cheap candy to tide the kids over
Ask George if you can borrow his medal!

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Piers.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Yes, Captain!

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: I heard your leave was approved.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Yes, I suppose it went rather well. It's all thanks to...

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: It's all thanks to that babyface of yours, lad.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: The brass occasionally want to put up a facade of caring about their subordinates. They call it good branding.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Haha, I guess the brass happened to be in a good mood.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: The mill back home stopped working and the old carpenter there broke his leg again, so my mother asked me home to help out.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Ten days of leave, minus eight days on the road. A day and a half is more than enough for me to deal with that rickety antique!

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: I left an extra half-day open, just in case my dad needs help tilling the other part of the field.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Oh right, I should pick up another dozen work gloves. The ones back home are past their prime.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Hmm. Is this... a shopping list?

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: That's right, Captain. Just so nothing is missing. I don't know when I'm going to get time off again.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Hopefully you've earned yourself a real medal or two by then.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Of course. All for Victoria!

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: That's the kind of ambition I want to see, lad.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: I once knew a bloke named Todd. He and I fought against those Spire Casters out on the frontier, and he earned himself a solid gold medal.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: What a beautiful thing that was, glittering as it hung on his chest. It shone so brightly nobody could take their eyes off it.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Our beloved Duke Windermere personally awarded him the medal, which is the highest of honors for any soldier. But, at the celebration banquet later on, old Todd had a bitter look on his face.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Can you guess why?

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Because he wasn't satisfied with the merits he earned?

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: No, no. It's much worse than that.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: He couldn't lift his mug to take a swig of beer. His hands got replaced with a pair of wooden prosthetics, hah!
The veteran officer grins, showing a mouthful of yellowed teeth.
The young soldier laughs dryly. He knows this is one of the officer's many poor jokes.
The wind is so strong on the deck that the soldier has to hold on to the brim of his hat, letting out a loud yet harmless sneeze.
No matter the season or weather, standing on the deck of a prancing high-speed battleship always makes one want to wrap himself in his coat.
The young soldier thinks to himself– Wells is in charge today; how many cans of rations did that pudgy, bald man swipe?
But, the creamy vegetable chowder he makes is without equal, and if fortune is on his side, that old bastard might even throw in a healthy serving of fowlbeast into the soup.
He figures that he should leave after the sun sets and he finishes dinner.
The mobile fortress they're stationed in has already reached Londinium's vicinity. When the weather is clear, they can even see the pinnacle of The Shard on the horizon.
After returning to the station, he'd board the logistics squad's transport vehicle and head to the nearest town first, where he'd be able to have a drink or two at the tavern.
In the early morning, there'd be cobblers heading into town to sell their wares. Two boxes of tobacco would let them hitch a ride.
The young soldier recalls those barns from back home, always filled with the fermented smell of composted straw.
Even now, that smell occasionally wafts to him in his dreams, making him want to pinch his nose. But at the same time, it represents a connection with his hometown.
If it only occurs occasionally, then so be it. He furrows his brows quietly, deciding not to continue deluding himself with these sentiments.
Even if it's only occasional, he doesn't want to experience that stench again. He must admit, that is always the biggest impediment every time he returns home.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Ugh, the fog's rising again. I'll never get used to Londinium's bloody weather.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Wasn't much better when we were stationed at Leithanien's outskirts, but at least you could enjoy a little sunshine in the afternoon.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Go. Tell the Captain, we can't see a thing at this weather observation outpost. Something's interfering with the radar too. We should head back.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Caster's forces are obediently maintaining formation, Gododdin moved his men further back. Other than the few familiar faces in the forward team, old Wellington's main force still hasn't shown up.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Other than our dear Duke Windermere, the remaining seven dukes are watching on from the sidelines. The patrol's over.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Sir, that Sarkaz...

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: None of our business. The brass always have their own agenda.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: But, I heard that Londinium's...

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Piers, I've been a soldier for over a decade. After drinking and playing cards, the most important thing I've picked up from being in the army is–

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Those rumors you hear are always bunkum and balderdash. Never pay any heed to them. The officers in the back have their eyes on the map and will take care of everything; ours is but to do and die.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Isn't it our duty... to defend Victoria?

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Only they can decide what Victoria is, boy. Our job is simply to follow orders.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: Go and head back. Our day of peace is over.

steps.name: Veteran Officer
steps.text: I ought to treat myself to a hot shower. This damn fog's making my bones ache.
Maybe things have been too stressful these days. The young soldier begins to thank himself for taking some time off to unwind.
The battlefield always puts people on edge, even more so when you don't know where the when or where war will break out, or who you can trust.
He thinks to himself, it's a bit clammy.
He lifts his hand to undo the first button of his shirt. Seeing as how his dear officer had just declared the end of the armistice, a little disregard for protocol shouldn't matter.

He thinks of the fireplace back home. A few years ago, he came home wearing a brand-new military outfit, unwilling to undo even a single button despite sweating profusely from the heat of hearth. For that, the young lass Shirley laughed at him for quite some time.
The young soldier curls the corner of his lips.

steps.name: Young Soldier
steps.text: Heh. That's why I didn't bring you your sappy romance novel. Payback.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Main cannon output is normal. Confirming target destroyed.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Begin preparations for the next phase. The dukes will react soon.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Your Highness.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Y-Your Highness!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hmm, a new face?

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Y-Yes! Your Highness, I was just promoted from the mercenary unit by the General!

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: It... It is the greatest honor... You've always been my...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's an honor to make your acquaintance as well. What is your name?

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: My name... My name is...

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: (whispers) I don't have a formal name... They just call me 'Elbow.'

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Uhh... Damn, I should've picked a name from a book.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'Elbow'... Why that name?

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: It's nothing, I just got burnt when I was drinking soup... I mean, it's a stupid story, hardly worth your attention, Your Highness...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You must've been holding your bowl too high.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: No! It was 'Plug'! That bastard ran into me! The next time I see him, I swear...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Your Highness.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Oh, I... I'm sorry, General, Your Highness.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You may leave. It seems you still have a lot of work to do.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I heard they're serving creamy vegetable chowder at the airship garrison tonight. Don't miss supper time.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Thank you, Your Highness Theresa.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: We...

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: 'When each battle ends, the Sarkaz have a home to return to.'

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: We'll be able to return to Kazdel soon, right?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I prefer to be with them rather than with the aristocrats of the Royal Court.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Each and every moment, the collective souls of the Sarkaz force me to my knees, immersing me in our long and painful history.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But they... these newly-grown children, give me a tangible sense of the future.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: And... what should we do with this future? Consign it to another round of wars sweeping across the land?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: When scorched earth spreads as far as the eye can see, will these new seedlings sprout as we hope?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hope is as weighty as ever, Manfred.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Your Highness...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: In accordance with the Military Commission's plans, a section of Londinium has been detached. As of right now, it has arrived at the designated location, parked between the main city and the dukes' encirclement.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It will become the cornerstone and launchpad of our next offensive, and this airship will also temporarily dock there.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The Duke of Windermere should soon receive news that her high-speed battleship has been destroyed, but she also cannot ignore the threat this airship poses, which in turn will help the Nachzehrer King's front develop.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: In accordance with the Regent's instructions, we must next...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Take a look outside, General.
Manfred turns to look out the window.
He is forced to admit that the carefully-planned flames burning before his eyes are... not as exhilarating as he had imagined.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The firelight is blinding.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Our war has finally broken out.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: According to the Military Commission's projections, the dukes will cautiously proceed with military operations within sixteen hours. We have already made our preparations.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, the war never ended.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It is not only ranks ripping through other ranks that is worthy of the name of war. Those eyes lurking behind the curtains, those curses whispered in the dead of night, those suppressed cries... are all war.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Those compatriots who perished alone in the barrens, those robes dragged across the ground during the Black Processions, those Kazdel bricks and tiles sealed away in a collector's glass display case... are also all war.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: War has always been a part of us. We simply... pushed it out for all to see once again.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Even if the flames of war were ignited in Victoria, Kazdel has always been a part of the battlefield. I've already made many plans with the General about this...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, Manfred, that's not what I was asking.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I simply observed that beneath our feet, the shadow of this airship covers all indiscriminately.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Put an end to it, General. If this ultimately is proven to be the only way for the Sarkaz...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Then, drown tears with tears, and bury suffering with suffering.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: This... is the only way.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I will carry out your will, Your Highness.

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: You see that?

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: No mistake about it. Looks like it came straight out of a storybook.

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: The harbinger of destruction. The prophet of turmoil. Nightmare given form...

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: You ever see that gloompincer as big as a mountain, lugging along its chest of perfume?

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Yup, just like Red-Nosed Humbert talked about.

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Nine said before, you're in no condition to be drinking.

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: I only had a sip! I don't have much time left. Leave me with my last bit of hope!

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: You still remember that night on the snowfield, right? Everyone was freezing to death, and Red-Nosed Humbert told us about a strange legend from his village–

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Sorry... I signed on in Victoria.

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Oh really? I thought...

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Yeah, Red-Nosed Humbert died back in Ursus. He was a good guy, took at least four of those Patrol Unit bastards with him.

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Damn it, you would've appreciated him and his stories. Gotta pour one out for him.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: You're drunk again, Romanich. How many times do I have to tell you? Hand over the flagon.

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Ma'am, I don't have much longer to live, c'mon...

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: You've still got a long life ahead of you, if you listen to the doctor.

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: I, I hate doctors! They're all liars, all of 'em!

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: I need these fluids... They let me see... (mutters softly)...

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: He's asleep again.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Toss him a blanket.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: We can't be too far from Londinium now.

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Yeah. If we're lucky, we'll be able to see those city walls in just over a week. It'd be faster if we could fix that piece-of-junk car.

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: You don't see Catastrophes too often around Londinium, but given the current situation, it's virtually impossible not to bump into any of the dukes' troops. And none of 'em are gonna welcome us.

steps.name: Uneasy Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Then, throw the Sarkaz on top...

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: We need to be even more cautious during our subsequent operations.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: We need to find our trapped people, whether they still think they're our people or not.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Getting everyone back together is difficult... but, we still feel the same pain and share the same sorrow. Those feelings never stop chasing us, and they force us to keep moving forward.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: I'm not saying that just to cope, but... this is the only thing we can do with full peace of mind–

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Let those Infected on the verge of despair know that they still have comrades out there, and that their lives aren't disposable.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Stay where you belong.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Nine.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm just getting a breath of fresh air.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Fine. I have my eye on you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Flames are burning... Out there, in the distance.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: They've been burning for some time now. Hopefully, it's just a patch of woods struck by lightning.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Our squad will cross over.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Lightning, huh...?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: I saw you were making stew back at camp.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I was just helping out the cook. She still had two baskets of potatoes to get through.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: I gave it a taste. Wasn't too bad.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Alina... I mean, an old friend once taught me a few things.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I thought I had forgotten it all.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: If you're still willing to play a part before facing justice, I won't stop you.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: But, you'd best remember who you are, Talulah. We'll be watching you. All of us.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Start packing up. It's time to go.

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Huh? I fell asleep? Damn it...

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: C'mon, Nine! Take pity on this old man and let me have another sip! Otherwise, I'm as good as dead today!

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Bah! Did you see that? The edge of the sky's blood red! Red-Nosed Humbert said...

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: He said that's a good omen... A good omen, I tell you!

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: He said that was... the other shore? Victory? Uhh, I don't exactly remember...

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Maybe, maybe...

steps.name: Crippled Reunion Fighter
steps.text: Maybe it means... Tomorrow will be a good day, my friends.
